info.description:
REST surface for the JAST core matching engine (JATS-style continuous
matching for Bursa Efek Indonesia). The engine knows only brokers
(participants), not individual investors, and stops at trade execution.


There are two authentication tiers, and they never mix:

- **Participant** (`/api/participant/*`, `/ws/participant/*`) — a broker
authenticates with its own key, stored hashed in the database and sent as
`X-Participant-Key`. Keys are issued and revoked per broker at runtime.
- **Admin** (`/api/admin/*`, `/ws/admin/*`) — the single static key from
configuration, sent as `X-API-Key`.

Orders enter only through POST /api/participant/orders. The order book can
be polled or streamed over WebSocket (documented, but not exercisable from
Swagger UI, since browsers cannot set headers on a WS handshake).
info.title: JAST Core API

get.description: Every broker's holdings, or one broker's when `participant` is given.

The exchange-wide rules in force right now, as the order path is
actually enforcing them.

**min_price** is the lowest price a limit order may carry, in rupiah.
It defaults to **50**, matching BEI's own minimum quotable price. Without
it the only price rule is `price > 0`, which lets a seller quote 58, then
5, then 1 — each one accepted, and each one resting in the book as the
best ask for whatever arrives next.

The remaining fields configure the circuit breakers. **emiten_halt_bps**
(default **3000** = 30%) is how far one emiten may move from its reference
price before trading in it halts; **index_halt_bps** (default **1200** =
12%) is how far the index may fall from its opening value before trading
halts market-wide; **halt_duration_seconds** (default **120**) is how long
either halt lasts.

Thresholds are in basis points — 1/100th of a percent, so 3000 is 30% —
because a threshold compared against a rupiah price stays in integer
arithmetic that way, with no rounding at the boundary that decides whether
a breaker trips.

put.description:
Changes the exchange-wide trading rules. The new value is persisted and
takes effect on the very next order — no restart, and it survives one.

Fields left out of the body keep their current value, so one parameter can
be changed without restating the rest. min_price must be greater than 0: a
floor of 0 is not a policy, it is the absence of the rule.

The halt thresholds must be between 1 and 10000 basis points, and the halt
duration between 1 and 86400 seconds. Both ends are enforced. A threshold
of 0 does not disable a breaker, it arms one that trips on the first trade
of the session; a threshold above 100% can never trip, leaving a breaker
that reads as protection and provides none.

400.description: A parameter is outside its permitted range

get.description:
Every announced, executed and cancelled aksi korporasi, newest first.

Cancelled actions are listed rather than hidden: participants were told
about them, so they are part of the instrument's history.

Pass `kode` to scope the listing to one instrument. The per-broker
movements an executed action caused are on the detail endpoint, not here —
they are a row per holder and would dominate a listing.

post.description:
Records an aksi korporasi that will take effect later. **Nothing moves
here** — no holding is restated and no wallet is credited until
POST /api/admin/corporate-actions/{id}/execute is called. That gap is the
point: an announced action can still be cancelled, and an executed one
cannot.

Four kinds, and the terms you send depend on which:
- **SPLIT** — `ratio_from`:`ratio_to`, e.g. 1:2 turns one share into two.
`ratio_to` must be greater than `ratio_from`.
- **REVERSE_SPLIT** — e.g. 2:1 turns two shares into one. `ratio_to` must
be *less* than `ratio_from`.
- **BONUS** — new shares issued free to holders. 2:3 hands the holder of
two shares a third.
- **DIVIDEND** — `amount` in rupiah per share held. No ratio.

Sending the wrong terms for the kind is rejected rather than ignored: a
dividend carrying a ratio means something was misunderstood, and accepting
it silently would carry that through to execution.

The instrument must already be trading. An action over a dormant one would
restate holdings nobody has.

400.description: Bad terms for the kind, or emiten not trading

get.description:
One aksi korporasi and every ledger movement it caused: which broker held
how many shares before it, how many after, and how much cash it received.

`entries` is empty for an action that has not executed. That is the honest
answer rather than an error — the action exists and is readable, nobody has
simply received anything from it yet.

The share totals are summed from the entries, not read off the instrument,
so this keeps reporting what *this* action did even after later actions have
moved the instrument on again.

400.description: Malformed id

post.description:
Abandons an announced action before it takes effect.

The row is kept, not deleted: participants were told about the action, so
its cancellation is part of the instrument's history, and removing it would
leave the record disagreeing with what the market was told.

Only an ANNOUNCED action can be cancelled — an executed one has already
moved every holder's ledger, and there is no undoing that from here.

400.description: Malformed id

post.description:
Applies an announced action to the ledgers. **This cannot be undone.**

A SPLIT, REVERSE_SPLIT or BONUS restates every holder's position by the
ratio and the instrument's `listed_shares` with it, in one transaction —
an instrument whose share count disagreed with the sum of its holders'
positions would make every valuation derived from it wrong. The price band's
anchor is restated by the inverse ratio at the same time, because the
instrument is worth the same immediately after a split as immediately
before it; an anchor left alone would auto-reject every order at the new
fair value.

A DIVIDEND credits each holder `amount` × shares held, and restates
nothing.

Shares are indivisible, so a ratio that does not divide a holding evenly
truncates — a 2:3 bonus on an odd holding drops the half share rather than
issuing one the action never authorised. Holdings are read as they stand at
execution; `record_date` is informational, since the engine keeps no
end-of-day snapshot.

Only an ANNOUNCED action can be executed. A second attempt is a 409, which
is what stops an action doubling every holding twice.

400.description: Malformed id, or the instrument has no holders

get.description:
Master data for every emiten, ordered by code. Price statistics are
deliberately excluded — computing them per row would be a query per
instrument. Use the detail endpoint for those.

post.description:
Registers an emiten and gives it an empty order book. It starts
**inactive** and is *not* tradeable — `is_active` is false and every order
against it is rejected.

That is deliberate: a listing is an instrument existing *and* its shares
being placed with the market. This endpoint does only the first. An
instrument whose shares sit nowhere has nobody who could sell it and no
offering price to quote against, so opening its book would advertise a
market that cannot trade.

To make it tradeable, run its offering with
`POST /api/admin/emiten/{kode}/ipo`. That is the only way an instrument
becomes active, and it is also where ipo_price is set — the offering price
is decided when the offering runs, not when the instrument is registered,
which is why this request does not take one.

A dormant instrument is fully readable in the meantime, and is excluded
from the composite index until it is priced.

400.description: Missing kode/nama, or listed_shares <= 0

get.description:
The same instrument detail the participant tier reads, on the admin key —
so oversight does not require holding a broker's credential. The admin list
omits price statistics — computing them per row would be a query per
instrument — so this endpoint is where they are read.

current_price, highest_price and lowest_price are strictly trade-derived and
are **null**, not 0, for an instrument that has never traded. reference_price
is what the instrument is valued at and falls back to ipo_price until the
first trade; price_source names which of the two it came from.

value is market capitalisation (reference price × total shares), derived on
read rather than stored, so it always reflects the latest trade.
free_float_percentage is the publicly tradeable share of the total and
always sums to 100 with unlisted_percentage.

post.description:
Takes an instrument that was registered through POST /api/admin/emiten —
and is therefore still **dormant** — public: it hands the shares to the
syndicate and opens the order book. This is the only way an instrument
becomes tradeable.

The body carries no share counts. listed_shares and unlisted_shares are the
instrument's own, fixed when it was registered — an offering decides who
underwrites it and at what price, not how many shares the company has. The
tranches must sum to exactly the listed_shares it already carries.

The syndicate rules are the same as POST /api/admin/ipo:
- each `underwriter` is a **broker code** that has been permitted to underwrite
- the tranches must sum to **exactly** the instrument's listed_shares
- every member is on equal terms; there is no lead

ipo_price becomes the instrument's reference price until it first trades. An
instrument that is already trading is rejected — a second offering would
issue its shares twice.

400.description: Bad syndicate, shares do not sum, unknown underwriter, or emiten already trading

post.summary: Run an IPO over a registered instrument

get.description:
Identical to the participant view: the index is one number the whole
exchange shares, and there is no broker-specific version of it. Offered
on the admin tier so an operator can read it with the key it already
holds, rather than having to issue itself a broker key.

503.description: Index has not been computed yet

post.description:
Writes the current level into the index history immediately, rather than
waiting for the next automatic capture.

Useful for marking a specific moment — the end of a session, or the state
just before an intervention — without depending on where the periodic
capture happens to fall.

Returns the level that was recorded. If nothing has been computed yet,
nothing is written and 503 is returned rather than an empty success.

503.description: Index has not been computed yet

get.description:
Identical to the participant view — the same series, offered on the
admin tier so an operator can read it with the key it already holds.

400.description: from or to is not RFC 3339

post.description:
Revalues the whole market immediately and refreshes the published level,
instead of waiting for the next trade to trigger it.

This exists for the case where the level is stale through no fault of the
market: a price read failed, or an instrument was listed while the index
could not reach the database. Ordinary operation needs no such call — the
index recomputes on every execution by itself.

Admin-only because it is an exchange operation, and because valuing the
entire market is real work that no broker should be able to schedule at
will.

Lists an instrument and hands its shares to the underwriting syndicate in
one step — an instrument whose shares sit nowhere is not yet an offering.

The syndicate is flat — every member takes a tranche on equal terms:
- each `underwriter` is a **broker code** that has been permitted to underwrite
- the tranches must sum to **exactly** listed_shares — a short sum leaves
shares in nobody's hands, an over-sum conjures shares that were never issued

ipo_price becomes the instrument's reference price until it first trades, so
it has a valuation and something to quote against from the moment it lists.
The allocation is one transaction: the audit rows and the share credits move
together or not at all.

400.description: Bad syndicate, shares do not sum, or unknown underwriter

get.description:
Every order ever submitted, newest first, optionally filtered by emiten,
participant, or status. This is the audit trail; the live book is served
by the orderbook endpoints.

400.description: Unknown emiten/participant, or bad status

get.description:
Every exchange participant, ordered by code. API keys are **not** included
and cannot be: only their hashes are stored. The prefix identifies which
key is in place without exposing it.

post.description:
Registers an exchange participant and issues its first API key.
The key is returned **once, in this response only** — it is stored as a
SHA-256 hash and cannot be retrieved again. A lost key is re-issued, not
recovered.

201.description: Created; contains the only copy of the key

400.description: Missing kode or nama

delete.description:
Removes the key. The next request carrying it is rejected immediately —
authentication reads the database rather than a cache, so revocation is
not delayed by an expiry.

400.description: Unknown participant

post.description:
Mints a new key and invalidates the previous one immediately. The key is
returned once and never again. The target broker travels in the body, not
the path, so no identifier lands in access or proxy logs.

201.description: The only copy of the new key

400.description: Unknown participant

get.description:
The raw execution log, newest first, optionally filtered by emiten or
participant. Each row is one buy order matched against one sell order.

Fills seen from a broker's own side. Omit `participant` to include every
broker. A broker that matched its own resting order appears twice for
that execution, once per side.

400.description: participant is required

get.description:
Every broker permitted to underwrite offerings, ordered by code.

An underwriter is a participant with a permission, not a firm of its own,
so kode and nama are that participant's — `kode` and `participant` are
always the same value. Allocated shares land in that broker's holdings,
because only a participant can trade them.

Members carry no rank: every underwriter in a syndicate is on equal terms.

post.description:
Grants an existing broker the right to underwrite offerings. That is all an
underwriter is — a participant with a permission — so the request carries
only the broker code: its name and code are the participant's already, and
are joined on read rather than stored twice.

The broker is also its trading identity: IPO allocations credit that
participant's holdings, so an underwriter without one could be handed
shares it could never sell.

A broker may be registered once. Registering it again is a 409.

400.description: Missing participant, or unknown participant

get.description: Every broker's cash balance, or one broker's when `participant` is given.

post.description:
Moves cash into or out of one broker's balance and returns the balance it
settles at. A positive `amount` credits the broker, a negative one debits
it; `0` is rejected.

Admin-only by design: a broker that could credit its own wallet could buy
without limit, so funding is an exchange operation.

A broker registered but never funded has no wallet row yet. This endpoint
creates it, so it opens a wallet and fills it in one call.

A debit is checked against **available** cash, not the stored balance:
cash already committed to resting buy orders cannot be withdrawn, or
those orders would be left unfunded when they fill. The rejection names
the most that may be withdrawn.

400.description: Missing participant, amount of 0, or a debit beyond available cash

post.summary: Fund or debit a broker's wallet

get.description:
Every instrument the authenticated broker holds, with the current market
value of each.

The broker is taken from the API key and this endpoint accepts no
`participant` parameter, so one broker cannot read another's positions.

value is derived from the latest trade price rather than stored, so it is
current even when this broker has not traded. It is null when the
instrument has never traded.

Master data plus all-time price statistics and derived valuations.

current_price, highest_price, lowest_price and value are **null**, not 0,
for an instrument that has never traded — no price exists yet, which is
not the same as a price of zero.

value is market capitalisation (current price × total shares), derived on
read rather than stored, so it always reflects the latest trade.
free_float_percentage is the publicly tradeable share of the total and
always sums to 100 with unlisted_percentage.

Executions aggregated into open/high/low/close bars with volume, newest
bar first. Buckets are UTC-aligned. Open and close follow execution
order, so two trades sharing a timestamp still resolve correctly.

400.description: Unsupported interval

get.description:
Every execution for an instrument, newest first. Build candles from this
client-side, or use the candles endpoint.

The exchange-wide price level, computed IHSG-style: the summed
free-float market capitalisation of every listed instrument, divided by
a divisor and scaled to a base of 100.

Each instrument is valued at its last traded price, falling back to its
IPO price until it has traded — the same reference price the emiten
detail endpoint reports. An instrument with neither is excluded rather
than counted as zero, which is why **members** may be lower than
**total**.

Weighting is by listed (free-float) shares, not total shares outstanding,
matching BEI's own methodology since 2021.

**divisor** is restated whenever an instrument lists, so the level does
not jump on an event where no price moved. It is returned so a client can
verify the level rather than trust it.

503.description: Index has not been computed yet

get.description:
Past index levels, newest first. Each point carries the market
capitalisation and divisor that produced it, so an old level stays
verifiable even after the divisor has since been restated.

Optional **from** and **to** bound the range, both RFC 3339 (for example
`2026-07-30T00:00:00Z`). An unparseable value is rejected with 400 rather
than silently ignored, since a filter that quietly does nothing returns a
page the caller will misread as the whole range.

400.description: from or to is not RFC 3339

get.description: Returns a paginated list of the current order books, ordered by emiten code.

Returns the book aggregated by price level. Bids are highest price
first; asks are lowest price first.

post.description:
Runs the order through continuous matching and returns the trades it
produced. A limit order with leftover quantity rests in the book (open);
a market order with leftover quantity is cancelled and never booked.
The order, its trades and the fills against the resting orders it
consumed are persisted in a single transaction.

A sell is rejected if the broker does not hold enough shares once its
resting sell orders are counted, so a position can never go negative.

**Auto-rejection.** A limit order priced outside the instrument's session
band is rejected and never reaches the book, so the price it asked for
never becomes a level anything else can match against. The band is
`reference_price ± emiten_halt_bps` (30% by default) and is anchored to the
session reference, not to the last trade — an anchor that moved with the
market would let the price walk out of the band one legal step at a time.
The rejection message quotes the permitted range.

**Circuit breaker.** A trade that prints at either edge of the band halts
the instrument for halt_duration_seconds (2 minutes by default). Orders
submitted during a halt are rejected with the resume time; the book stays
readable and resting orders keep their time priority. Trading reopens by
itself — no request is needed.

200.description: Order processed: the resulting order state and any trades

400.description: Unknown emiten/participant, bad side/type, qty <= 0, price <= 0 for a limit order, insufficient shares, an inactive emiten, a price outside the permitted band, or a halted instrument

post.description:
Withdraws an order that is still resting in the book and releases
what it had reserved — shares for a sell, cash for a buy — so the
broker can use them again immediately. The quantity that already
filled stays filled; only the remainder is withdrawn.

Only the broker that placed the order may cancel it. An order that
has already filled or been cancelled is not resting, so it cannot be
withdrawn and the request is rejected.

The book row and the stored order are cancelled in one step, and the
updated book is published to subscribers. A cancel produces no trade
and therefore moves no price.

Cancelling is allowed while the instrument is halted: a halt stops new
orders from arriving, it does not trap the ones already resting.

200.description: Order cancelled: its final state and the quantity released

400.description: Unknown emiten/participant, order_id <= 0, an order that is not resting, or an order belonging to another participant

get.description:
Every fill for the authenticated broker, newest first, seen from its own
side — so `side` and `counterparty` are relative to the caller.

The broker is taken from the API key. This endpoint accepts no
`participant` parameter, so one broker cannot read another's fills.

The authenticated broker's current cash balance.

The broker is taken from the API key and this endpoint accepts no
`participant` parameter, so one broker cannot read another's balance.

Upgrades to a WebSocket connection. On connect the server sends a full
snapshot — the same shape as GET /api/participant/orderbook/{kode}, tagged
with type "update" — then a fresh full snapshot every time this emiten's
book changes. The stream is outbound-only; orders are never accepted over it.

The identical stream is available to admin at /ws/admin/orderbook/{kode};
only the credential differs.

Not exercisable from Swagger UI, because it is not plain HTTP and browsers
cannot set headers on a WS handshake. Connect with a WebSocket client at

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket connection. On connect the server sends a full
snapshot — the same shape as GET /api/participant/orderbook/{kode}, tagged
with type "update" — then a fresh full snapshot every time this emiten's
book changes. The stream is outbound-only; orders are never accepted over it.

The identical stream is available to admin at /ws/admin/orderbook/{kode};
only the credential differs.

Not exercisable from Swagger UI, because it is not plain HTTP and browsers
cannot set headers on a WS handshake. Connect with a WebSocket client at
ws://localhost:8080/ws/participant/orderbook/BBCA.
